meaning: The hardware counters inside a processor core, each of which counts one kind of event such as a clock cycle or a retired instruction.
One page of readings for one workload on one machine: throughput, where the CPU's slots went, what the GPU tools showed, and how it was counted.
The Linux tool that reads the processor's counters; perf stat runs a program and prints the totals.
One beat of a processor core; counters and top-down shares are expressed per cycle.
One of the smaller internal steps a core breaks each program instruction into; Intel writes uOp.
The part of a core that predicts the next instructions, fetches them and decodes them into micro-operations.
The part of a core that executes micro-operations in its arithmetic and memory units.
The last pipeline stage, where the results of executed micro-operations are made final in program order.
Running instructions after a branch before knowing which way the branch goes, on a guess.
Throwing away the micro-operations started after a wrong branch guess and restarting from the right place.
One chance, in one clock cycle, to pass one micro-operation from the front end to the back end; a core has a fixed number per cycle.
The number of slots per cycle of a core, for example 10 on the Cortex-X925 and Neoverse V3.
A method that sorts every slot of every cycle into one of four buckets to show where a core's capacity went.
The share of slots that carried a micro-operation which finished: the useful work.
The share of slots that carried work thrown away after a wrong branch guess.
The share of slots left empty because the front end had no micro-operation ready.
The share of slots left empty because the back end could not accept another micro-operation.
The part of back-end bound in which the core is waiting for data to be loaded or stored.
The part of back-end bound in which execution units are busy or operations wait on each other's results.
Finished instructions divided by clock cycles, a one-number summary of how much a core gets done per beat.
Arm's adjustment that moves the slots lost while recovering from a wrong branch guess from front-end bound to bad speculation.
The Arm event that counts cycles the front end spent recovering from a flush, used by the Neoverse V3, Cortex-X925 and Cortex-A725 formulas.
Two hardware threads sharing one processor core.
The Arm processors AWS designs for EC2; Graviton3, 4 and 5 use the Neoverse V1, V2 and V3 cores.
An EC2 instance with no virtual machine layer between the operating system and the hardware.
One function launched on the GPU, such as a matrix multiply; unrelated to the operating system's kernel.
The GPU's processing unit, repeated many times across the chip.
The units inside each GPU multiprocessor that do the matrix arithmetic of training and inference.
The GPU units that find what each camera ray hits when an image is rendered.
The percent of time in the sample period during which at least one kernel was running on the GPU.
NVIDIA's fleet monitoring service, which adds SM activity, tensor activity and memory activity per GPU.
The fraction of time at least one group of threads was active on a GPU multiprocessor.
The fraction of cycles the GPU's tensor pipeline was active.
NVIDIA's profiler that puts CPU samples, GPU calls and kernels of one application on a single timeline.
NVIDIA's profiler for one GPU kernel, reporting throughput against the GPU's maximum and a roofline chart.
A chart of a kernel's achieved speed against arithmetic per byte of memory moved, under a roof whose sloped part is the memory bandwidth limit and whose flat part is the peak compute limit.
